text:
Sebastian Cossa gets the net tonight against Colorado after Karel Vejmelka was pulled on Monday, and it's a chance he needs. The 15th overall pick in 2021, drafted by Detroit out of the Edmonton Oil Kings and now in Utah, has a 4-2-1 record but an .864 save percentage. He has allowed 5.0 goals more than his shots usually produce, 9th percentile among goalies.

The breakdown is stranger than the total. On high-danger shots he's been good: .750 against a league .685. The damage is in the middle band, where he's at .759 against a league .863, about 6.4 goals worse than expected on shots most goalies handle. In 176 shots, a split like that can be a small-sample quirk as much as a flaw, but it showed up in his last two appearances, five goals each against Montreal and Vegas.

He has a short NHL track record, and our talent range still puts his true save rate near league average. His last stop before the NHL was 40 AHL games for Grand Rapids at .913. Tonight's test is a hard one: Mackenzie Blackwood in the other crease and the Avalanche in front of him.
